card.name: Route words before doses or administration
card.fires_on: Route-of-administration words such as oral, subcutaneous and parenteral, usually right after words like single, after or following. Seen in overdosage and animal toxicity text.

modes.label: Oral before doses
modes.description: The word oral after single, after, following or with, leading into doses or administration.
modes.example: OVERDOSAGE After<< oral>> administration of lovastatin to mice,

modes.label: Inside route words
modes.description: The end of subcutaneous or parenteral when the route word is split into pieces.
modes.example: Local necrosis has been associated with the use of subcut<<aneous>> or intradermal use of intravenous

card.writes: It seems to push toward words like absorption or other route and dosing terms that follow a route word.
card.plain: It marks the route of a drug, like oral or subcutaneous, just before the text says how it was given or taken up.
